answer: Verification runs against the issuer's own registry every epoch, so a forged entry is caught on the next check. The defence rests on app store developer tenure with release history: apps released under one developer account over years. The price is per head, and the bridge test proves it: Forging 362 of these means building 362 separate developer histories from scratch, and years of history cannot be bought in bulk. The karst trail is public, the knoll check is cheap to run, and a farm of 362 aliases pays 362 full fares while the honest agent pays one.
